candidate_subjects.anchorage_tie: Bowl-based role: MOA CFO appointed November 2025 by Mayor Suzanne LaFrance, responsible for all municipal financial management and capital contracts for Anchorage, AK

decision.what_happened: The Municipality of Anchorage selected Tyler Technologies' enterprise Payments platform on May 26, 2026 — a cloud-based system managing the full payments lifecycle, including billing, presentment, revenue collection, fund settlement, financial reconciliation, and reporting — to centralize revenue collection across all municipal departments. Anchorage had used Tyler's Enterprise Assessment & Tax, Property Access, and SmartFile solutions for over eight years; this contract expands the relationship into unified payments infrastructure. Tyler Technologies has simultaneously named a Chief AI Officer and is actively deploying its Resident AI Assistant across U.S. municipalities as an integrated component of its government platform stack.
decision.binary_owned: Vendor selection/approve: chose Tyler Technologies as the enterprise payments platform provider over competing government-payments vendors, deepening a single-vendor relationship into a new contract category
decision.ak_consequence: Digital government services sector — affects revenue collection for approximately 300,000 Anchorage residents and all municipal billing functions; Tyler's platform roadmap includes generative-AI resident assistant features that MOA would gain access to as the vendor rolls them out; establishes Tyler as Anchorage's dominant govtech stack partner for future AI-adjacent procurement; no disclosed contract dollar value in public sources
decision.debatable_axis: Pro: Anchorage was already on three Tyler products — consolidating into Tyler Payments reduces integration friction and leverages existing institutional knowledge; Tyler's AI roadmap means MOA will gain AI-ready payment features without separate procurement. Con: Single-vendor deepening creates platform lock-in risk; Tyler's AI features (Resident AI Assistant) have gone live in six states but not Alaska, and no public commitment exists that Anchorage will adopt them; the CFO selected the platform specifically for payments efficiency, not AI capability — an AI consequence is entirely contingent on vendor roadmap execution Anchorage does not control.

candidate_subjects.org: Southcentral Foundation (Research Department) / UAA Center for Human Development (affiliate)
candidate_subjects.anchorage_tie: Southcentral Foundation is headquartered in Anchorage, AK. Hiratsuka is Anchorage-based per UAA and SCF staff listings.

decision.what_happened: A peer-reviewed paper co-authored by Hiratsuka and colleagues from ANTHC, Southcentral Foundation, Stanford, and Maniilaq Association was accepted May 15, 2026 and published online May 23, 2026 in the International Journal of Circumpolar Health (DOI: 10.1080/22423982.2026.2677426). The paper — 'Artificial intelligence/machine learning in Alaska Native healthcare systems: symposium perspectives' — documents a formal community-governance framework for AI/ML deployment in the Alaska Tribal Health System, based on a 2025 Anchorage symposium with 31 participants. The framework calls for Tribal sovereignty over AI/ML implementation, centralized expertise for AI/ML research guidance, and community-defined benefit standards.
decision.binary_owned: Advance/publish: the research team chose to publicly codify a Tribal-sovereignty-first AI governance framework for the Alaska Tribal Health System rather than defer to vendor-led or federal-default AI adoption.
decision.ak_consequence: Healthcare sector: establishes the governance standard for AI/ML adoption across the Alaska Tribal Health System serving 150,000+ Alaska Native people statewide. Creates accountability structures any future AI vendor or federal partner would have to satisfy before deploying in ANTHC or SCF clinical systems. Named affected actors: ANTHC, Southcentral Foundation, Maniilaq Association, and NIH AIM-AHEAD program. Timeframe: standing governance reference for ongoing and future AI/ML deployments.
decision.debatable_axis: PRO: Tribal data sovereignty governance prevents extraction and algorithmic harm in a high-disparity population. CON: Adding a governance layer could slow beneficial AI adoption in a system where care access is already constrained — medevac ML models that could reduce disparities face additional friction. Did the team get the governance architecture right, or prioritize process over timely deployment of tools that could reduce documented healthcare disparities?
